subject: chemistry

concepts.title: Classification of Alcohols and Phenols
concepts.definition: Alcohols carry -OH groups on sp3 carbon while phenols have -OH straight on the ring; both families are sorted by how many -OH groups are present and how substituted that carbon is.
concepts.formula: R-CH2OH (1 deg), R2-CHOH (2 deg), R3-COH (3 deg)
concepts.key_idea: Classification varies with whether the -OH is on a primary, secondary, or tertiary carbon.
question_patterns: classify the following as primary, secondary or tertiary alcohols
identify if the given alcohol is allylic or benzylic
how are alcohols categorized based on hydroxyl group count
is this a monohydric or dihydric alcohol
determine the degree of the alcohol

solution_steps.explain: Locate the carbon atom directly bonded to the hydroxyl (-OH) group.
Count how many other carbon atoms are directly attached to the hydroxyl-bearing carbon.
One carbon is primary (1°), two is secondary (2°), and three is tertiary (3°).

concepts.title: IUPAC Nomenclature of Alcohols
concepts.definition: A systematic method of naming alcohols by replacing the 'e' of the parent alkane with the suffix 'ol' and indicating the -OH position with the lowest possible locant.
concepts.key_idea: The parent chain must be indeed the longest carbon chain containing the hydroxyl group.
question_patterns: give the IUPAC name of the following compound
write the IUPAC name for
what is the systematic name of this alcohol
name the compound according to IUPAC rules
provide the IUPAC designation for the structure

solution_steps.explain: Select the longest continuous carbon chain that includes the -OH group.
Number the carbons starting from the end closer to the -OH group to give it the lowest locant.
Name and number any alkyl or functional groups attached to the parent chain.
Combine the substituent names (alphabetically) with the parent alkane name, changing the suffix to 'ol'.

concepts.title: Boiling Point Trends in Alcohols
concepts.definition: Alcohols boil well above hydrocarbons of about the same molar mass because their molecules hydrogen-bond to each other.
concepts.key_idea: Hydrogen bonding increases boiling points; branching decreases them by reducing surface area.
question_patterns: arrange the following in increasing order of boiling points
why do alcohols have higher boiling points than ethers
explain the effect of branching on the boiling point of alcohols
compare the boiling points of ethanol and propane
which isomer has the highest boiling point

solution_steps.explain: Compare the number of carbon atoms; more carbons generally mean higher van der Waals forces.
Identify the presence of -OH groups which allow for strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
For isomers, the more branched the chain, the lower the boiling point due to decreased surface area.

concepts.title: Acid-Catalysed Hydration of Alkenes
concepts.definition: The addition of water to an alkene with an acid catalyst to produce an alcohol, following Markovnikov's rule.
concepts.key_idea: In Markovnikov addition, the hydroxyl group attaches to the more substituted carbon of the double bond.
question_patterns: predict the product of acid catalysed hydration of propene
write the mechanism for the hydration of ethene
what happens when an alkene reacts with water and acid
show the synthesis of propan-2-ol from propene
apply Markovnikov's rule to alkene hydration

solution_steps.explain: The alkene double bond attacks a hydronium ion to form a stable carbocation.
A water molecule attacks the carbocation.
A proton is removed from the oxonium ion to yield the final alcohol.

concepts.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation of Alkenes
concepts.definition: A two-step reaction where diborane adds to an alkene followed by oxidation with hydrogen peroxide to yield an anti-Markovnikov alcohol.
concepts.key_idea: The net result is indeed the addition of water in an anti-Markovnikov fashion.
question_patterns: explain hydroboration-oxidation with an example
how to prepare a primary alcohol from an unsymmetrical alkene
predict the product of propene reacting with BH3 then H2O2/NaOH
why is hydroboration-oxidation considered anti-Markovnikov
convert an alkene to an alcohol without carbocation rearrangement

solution_steps.explain: Boron attaches to the less substituted carbon of the double bond.
Hydrogen peroxide in basic medium replaces the boron atom with a hydroxyl group.
The hydroxyl group ends up on the less substituted carbon, giving the anti-Markovnikov alcohol.

concepts.title: Synthesis of Alcohols using Grignard Reagents
concepts.definition: The reaction of an organomagnesium halide with a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) followed by hydrolysis to form an alcohol.
concepts.key_idea: Methanal gives 1° alcohols, other aldehydes give 2° alcohols, and ketones give 3° alcohols.
question_patterns: how to prepare propan-1-ol using a Grignard reagent
predict the product of methyl magnesium bromide and propanone
what alcohol is formed from methanal and ethyl magnesium chloride
show the reaction of a Grignard reagent with an aldehyde
synthesize a tertiary alcohol from a ketone

solution_steps.explain: The alkyl group of the Grignard reagent attacks the carbonyl carbon.
The oxygen becomes an OMgX group.
Addition of water/acid converts the OMgX group into an OH group.

concepts.title: Acidity of Phenols
concepts.definition: Phenols are acidic because the phenoxide ion they form is stabilised when the negative charge spreads over the benzene ring.
concepts.key_idea: Phenols are indeed more acidic than alcohols because of resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion.
question_patterns: why is phenol more acidic than ethanol
explain the effect of nitro groups on phenol acidity
arrange substituted phenols in order of acid strength
draw resonance structures of phenoxide ion
compare the acidity of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol

solution_steps.explain: Check for electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) like -NO2 or electron-donating groups (EDG) like -CH3.
EWGs stabilize the negative charge on the phenoxide ion, increasing acidity.
EDGs destabilize the phenoxide ion, decreasing acidity.

concepts.title: Lucas Test for Alcohols
concepts.definition: The Lucas test mixes concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl2: a cloudy layer appears at different speeds for primary, secondary or tertiary alcohols, which is how they are told apart.
concepts.key_idea: Tertiary alcohols react immediately, secondary after 5 minutes, and primary only on heating.
question_patterns: how to distinguish between propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol
what is the Lucas reagent
describe the observation for a tertiary alcohol in Lucas test
identify the alcohol class using HCl and ZnCl2
why do tertiary alcohols react fastest in the Lucas test

solution_steps.explain: Mix the alcohol with concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl2.
Note the time taken for the solution to become cloudy due to alkyl halide formation.
Immediate turbidity indicates tertiary, within five minutes indicates secondary, and only on heating indicates primary.

concepts.title: Dehydration of Alcohols to Alkenes
concepts.definition: The elimination of a water molecule from an alcohol using a protic acid at high temperatures to form an alkene.
concepts.key_idea: Ease of dehydration follows the order: Tertiary > Secondary > Primary.
question_patterns: write the mechanism of dehydration of ethanol
predict the major product of dehydration of butan-2-ol
what is the order of ease of dehydration of alcohols
how is ethene prepared from ethanol
explain the role of acid in alcohol dehydration

solution_steps.explain: The alcohol oxygen is protonated by the acid catalyst.
A water molecule leaves, forming a carbocation (slowest step).
A proton is removed from an adjacent carbon to form the double bond.

concepts.title: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
concepts.definition: The reaction of phenol with chloroform with sodium hydroxide to introduce an aldehyde group at the ortho position.
concepts.key_idea: Salicylaldehyde is the primary product of this electrophilic substitution.
question_patterns: write the equation for Reimer-Tiemann reaction
how is salicylaldehyde prepared from phenol
what reagents are used in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction
identify the product of phenol reacting with CHCl3 and NaOH
explain the synthesis of ortho-hydroxybenzaldehyde

solution_steps.explain: Phenol reacts with chloroform and alkali to form a substituted benzal chloride intermediate.
The intermediate is hydrolyzed by the base to form the aldehyde group.
Salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is formed as the major product at the ortho position.

concepts.title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
concepts.definition: A laboratory method for preparing both symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers by reacting an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide via an SN2 mechanism.
concepts.key_idea: Primary alkyl halides give the best yields; tertiary halides result in elimination (alkenes).
question_patterns: how to prepare diethyl ether using Williamson synthesis
predict the product of sodium ethoxide and methyl bromide
why can't tertiary alkyl halides be used to make ethers in this reaction
synthesize t-butyl methyl ether correctly
write the reaction for Williamson synthesis of anisole

solution_steps.explain: Select a primary alkyl halide and a sodium alkoxide.
The alkoxide ion attacks the alkyl halide carbon, displacing the halide ion.
The desired ether R-O-R' is formed along with sodium halide (NaX) as a byproduct.

concepts.title: Cleavage of Ethers by Hydrogen Halides
concepts.definition: The chemical breakdown of ethers using concentrated HI or HBr, where the C-O bond is broken to form an alcohol and an alkyl halide.
concepts.key_idea: With mixed ethers, the halide typically forms with the smaller alkyl group via SN2, unless a tertiary group is present (SN1).
question_patterns: predict the products of reaction of methoxyethane with HI
what happens when anisole reacts with HI
explain the mechanism of ether cleavage with HI
identify products when t-butyl methyl ether reacts with HI
which bond breaks in alkyl aryl ethers with HX

solution_steps.explain: The ether oxygen is protonated by the hydrogen halide.
The halide ion attacks the less hindered carbon (SN2) or the carbon forming a stable carbocation (SN1).
An alcohol and an alkyl halide are formed; the halide bonds to the smaller alkyl group in mixed ethers.

concepts.title: Molecular Mass of Alkanols
concepts.definition: Calculating the total molecular weight of a saturated aliphatic monohydric alcohol based on its carbon count.
concepts.key_idea: The general formula for alkanols is CnH2n+1OH.
question_patterns: calculate the molecular mass of propanol
what is the molar mass of an alcohol with 4 carbons
find the weight of one mole of ethanol
determine the molecular mass of pentan-1-ol
what is the result in this molecular mass of alkanols problem

solution_steps.explain: Identify 'n' from the name (e.g., propanol, n=3).
Using the formula 2n + 2.
Add masses of C, H, and O (16).

worked_examples.question: Using Molecular Mass of Alkanols, compute the result for carbon_count = 3.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Determine carbon count: n = carbon_count = 3.0 Step 2: Calculate hydrogen count: h = 2 * n + 2 = 8.0 Step 3: Sum atomic masses: mass = (12 * n) + (1 * h) + 16 = 60.0 Final result: 60.0

worked_examples.question: Using Molecular Mass of Alkanols, compute the result for carbon_count = 4.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Determine carbon count: n = carbon_count = 4.0 Step 2: Calculate hydrogen count: h = 2 * n + 2 = 10.0 Step 3: Sum atomic masses: mass = (12 * n) + (1 * h) + 16 = 74.0 Final result: 74.0

solution_template.explain: Numbering from right gives -OH at C2.
